answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring every identity to scarce hardware: each participant must sign through an enclave whose key is fused in at the factory, and the registry counts how many distinct enclave roots stand behind each identity. Software clones are free, so a farmer can mint endless copies, but a small prism of a few hundred physical chips splits the swarm into countable roots, and duplicate claims on one root get caught at the summit checkpoint of each epoch. A stray raven with no enclave behind it is quarantined and paid nothing until real hardware vouches for it.
